title: Mass on a spring

narration.transcript: a block on a spring, filmed from the side

reference.basis: striped bar below has no stated length

slow_motion.evidence: no caption or narration indicates slow motion; animation plays as recorded

subjects.description: small green rectangular block hanging from a vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A green block hangs from a vertical spring attached to a fixed support above. It moves up and down with small amplitude about equilibrium for the whole clip, with no release or catch visible.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: Motion is on a vertical straight line with ~0.7 s period about a mid-point and slowly shrinking peaks, classic light-damped spring-mass. In air on Earth some velocity-dependent loss is expected. Candidates go from ideal to linear viscous to linear plus quadratic drag to identify the loss law.

critique.finding: The block bobs around {s_eq}, getting stiffer farther out with {beta} and losing energy to air with {cq}. It still drifts a little from low to high, so this only partly captures the motion.
critique.headline: Block rides stiffening spring with gentle air drag.
critique.why_it_won: It lets stiffness grow away from center and damps fast motion with air drag, so it stays near zero while simpler springs swing wildly.

preRevision.revision_idea: Add a small cubic stiffening to the spring force. The misses keep a steady wave at the bounce rhythm, suggesting the real frequency shifts as the swing shrinks in a way linear stiffness cannot follow.

headline: Block rides stiffening spring with gentle air drag.
finding: The block bobs around 67.157 ± 0.023 px, getting stiffer farther out with 0.005073 ± 0.000040 1/(s² px²) and losing energy to air with 0.0020824 ± 0.0000052 1/px. It still drifts a little from low to high, so this only partly captures the motion.

eyeball.law_in_words: vertical mass on spring about equilibrium with linear viscous damping: second time derivative of position equals -omega0^2 times displacement from s_eq minus gamma times velocity
